about: Machine-readable index of the statements the app displays. Levels follow docs/objective.md (1 Established, 2 Derived, 3 Hypothesis, 4 Open). Every statement names the cards that back it; the app shows their current verdicts from verify/ledger/latest.json. The app reads this file and never writes it.

ortho.inner-is-sum.text: The inner product is a sum of signed contributions: ⟨u,v⟩ = Σ uᵢvᵢ in Rⁿ, and ⟨f,g⟩ = ∫ f(t)g(t) dt for functions.

ortho.pythagoras.text: ‖u+v‖² = ‖u‖² + ‖v‖² + 2⟨u,v⟩, so u ⟂ v exactly when Pythagoras holds.

ortho.shadow.text: The shadow of v on u is (⟨u,v⟩/⟨u,u⟩)u. It vanishes exactly when ⟨u,v⟩ = 0, and the residual v − shadow is exactly perpendicular to u: an exact construction, so any nonzero remainder on screen is floating-point error.

ortho.rotation-invariance.text: Applying the same rotation R to both vectors changes every coordinate but not the inner product: (Ru)·(Rv) = u·v.

ortho.screen-distorts.text: A projection onto a screen or a coordinate plane does not preserve angles: an orthogonal pair can look oblique, and an oblique pair can look perpendicular.

ortho.signature.text: For a basis, zero cross terms (Gram = I), independent projection coefficients, Parseval additivity and residual ⟂ retained part all hold together when the basis is orthonormal.

ortho.trig-full-period.text: Over one full period, distinct sines and cosines have zero inner product: the Gram matrix of {cos kt, sin kt} is π·I.

ortho.discrete.text: Sampled at N equally spaced points on [0, 2π), two waves give orthogonal vectors exactly when their root-of-unity sums cancel; for cos mt and cos nt that means N divides neither m − n nor m + n. The condition m + n < N is sufficient for the waves used here, not the definition.

ortho.samples-to-integral.text: As the number of samples grows, the scaled sample sum (L/N) Σ f(tⱼ)g(tⱼ) approaches ∫ f g.

ortho.null-later.text: In an indefinite geometry a nonzero vector can have q(v) = 0 (a null vector). This is a different zero from orthogonality, compared later and never merged with it (Gate 3, H1-2).

ortho.camera.text: Orbiting the camera moves neither vector, so their inner product and true angle do not change. Only their two-dimensional projection on the screen changes, and a projection need not preserve angles.

ortho.interval.text: The domain is part of the inner product. For the basis cos kt/√π, sin kt/√π: G = I at L = 2π and G = 2I at L = 4π (orthogonal, not unit length); at other L some cross terms appear while others can stay zero.

coef.basis.text: The waves e_k(t) = e^{2πikt} are orthonormal on [0, 1]: ⟨e_j, e_k⟩ = ∫₀¹ e_j(t) conj(e_k(t)) dt = δ_jk.

coef.projection.text: A Fourier coefficient is a projection: f̂(k) = ⟨f, e_k⟩ = ∫₀¹ f(t) e^{−2πikt} dt. Geometrically it is the centroid of f wound around the circle at frequency k.

coef.independence.text: Because ⟨e_j, e_k⟩ = δ_jk, each coefficient is isolated: every other component contributes exactly 0 to ⟨f, e_k⟩.

coef.removal.text: Removing the k-th component of a real signal lowers ‖f‖² by exactly 2|f̂(k)|² (the ±k pair) and leaves every other coefficient unchanged.

coef.crosstalk.text: In a non-orthogonal basis the naive projections ⟨f, ẽ_k⟩ leak into one another: the Gram matrix leaves I, and Σ⟨f, ẽ_k⟩ẽ_k no longer rebuilds f.

coef.arrows.text: For real signals, ⟨f, g⟩ = Σ_k (√2 f̂(k))·(√2 ĝ(k)): the dot product of the coefficient arrows is the inner product of the waves, exactly.

coef.sampled.text: Sampled at N points, (1/N) Σ f(t_j)g(t_j) = Σ over N | k+l of f̂(k)ĝ(l). The terms with k + l ≠ 0 are aliasing; for harmonics up to K they vanish once N > 2K, and the sum equals ⟨f, g⟩.

coef.interval.text: The domain is part of the inner product. For the basis √2 cos 2πkt, −√2 sin 2πkt the Gram matrix is I on [0, 1] and 2I on [0, 2]; on other intervals some cross terms appear while others stay zero.

H1.text: Why orthogonality keeps appearing as a structural mechanism across representations (Nadia's hypothesis H1). The established consequences above are what an investigation of it can build on.

H2.pattern.text: Candidate pattern: Object → Representation → Transformation → Invariant → Decomposition → Geometry, plus what became visible, hidden or lost (Nadia's hypothesis H2).

zero.pair.text: v + w = 0 exactly when w = −v. Every nonzero v has such a partner, so one zero reading comes from a whole family of pairs of nonzero vectors.

zero.ensemble.text: A resultant can be exactly zero while every contribution is nonzero: four equal contributions toward the corners of a regular tetrahedron sum to 0. Any n − 1 contributions fix the last one, m_n = −(m_1 + … + m_{n−1}), so many configurations give the same zero.

zero.twist.text: Turning two contributions together about the line of their sum leaves their sum unchanged, so the resultant stays exactly what it was.

zero.first-moment.text: F(R) = Σ m_i (r_i − R) = M (R_CM − R), with M = Σ m_i and R_CM = Σ m_i r_i / M. With every mass positive, F(R) = 0 at R = R_CM and nowhere else.

zero.cm-shift.text: Shifting every mass by the same step moves the balancing point R_CM by that step.

backbone.primary.text: What appears as zero, cancellation, or balance in one representation may be evidence of an underlying geometric constraint.

idea.hidden-family.text: A single observed zero may correspond to a nontrivial family of hidden states.

Q.cancellation-information.text: What information is contained in the cancellation state itself?

Q.zero-inference.text: What can be inferred from the zero state while it remains zero?

Q.zero-generators.text: When presented with a zero-valued result, can we determine the hidden rules or structure that generated that zero?

Q.pairA.text: Are proton cancellation and mass balance two unrelated constructions, or do they admit a common representation?

quantum.sz-zero.text: A zero-valued observable can fail to uniquely determine a quantum state. For two spin-½ particles, (|↑↓⟩ + |↓↑⟩)/√2 and (|↑↓⟩ − |↓↑⟩)/√2 both give S_z = 0 with certainty, yet S² gives 2ħ² for the first and 0 for the second.

zero.not-identifying.text: A zero-valued measurement need not uniquely determine the underlying state: F(x) = 0 need not uniquely determine x. In the measurement maps examined here, one zero output can correspond to multiple underlying states or configurations.

zero.linear-preserves.text: If Σ v_i = 0, then Σ A v_i = A Σ v_i = 0 for every linear map A. Doubling every vector is such a map, and it preserves a bilinear form only when the form is 0.

zero.no-preserved-form.text: Zero-resultant preservation alone does not identify a particular preserved bilinear or metric form.

Q.zero-distinguishable.text: When a measurement is zero, what additional structure remains distinguishable?

Q.additional-relations.text: What additional preserved relations are needed to identify the geometry?

zero.shared-form.text: Under the representations currently used, both systems can exhibit a zero-sum vector relation: Σ_j m_j = 0 for the contributions, and Σ_i u_i = 0 with u_i = m_i (r_i − R_CM) for the masses.

quantum.not-reconstructed.text: Stage 2b establishes that the same zero measurement does not imply the same underlying quantum state. It does not establish that the hidden state can be reconstructed from the zero alone: the second observable, S², supplied the additional information.

Q.pairA-transfer.text: Does the shared zero-sum form preserve enough additional structure for knowledge from one system to constrain the other?

Q.zero-geometry-broader.text: Is zero preservation sufficient to identify a geometry in some broader sense?

Q.zero-internal-inference.text: What information, if any, can be inferred from the internal structure of a zero state without perturbing it into a nonzero state?

construction.r4-tetra.text: An orthogonal basis in R^4 can project into a 3-dimensional subspace as four equal tetrahedral vectors whose sum is zero.

construction.r4-derived.text: higher-dimensional orthogonal organization → lower-dimensional zero-sum organization

construction.r4-stage2.text: Stage 2 tetrahedral cancellation ← exact realization of projected R4 orthonormal basis

construction.r4-general.text: For every n ≥ 2, the n orthonormal basis vectors of R^n projected onto 1⊥ are the vertices of a regular simplex with zero sum.

construction.paira-bridge.text: Exact special-case bridge: Equal-mass centering of the standard basis produces the same regular-simplex zero configuration as projection of an orthonormal basis onto 1⊥.

construction.centering-operator.text: C_G = I − 1 1ᵀ G / (1ᵀ G 1), for positive diagonal G, is idempotent, kills 1, is G-self-adjoint, and contains T′ (G = I) and weighted mass centering (G = diag(m)) exactly.

qacp.cancellation.text: The zero is produced by two nonzero vectors in the Hilbert space cancelling exactly.

qacp.obstruction.text: The zero-producing structure alone (state, the two contribution operators, inner products) cannot distinguish the triplet and singlet zeros: a unitary commuting with both contribution operators maps one internal-zero configuration onto the other.

qacp.exchange.text: With the canonical exchange P of the two particles, P c1 = ε c2 with ε = +1 for |1,0⟩ and ε = −1 for |0,0⟩; ε equals the state's exchange parity.
